thread:
sam: quick question — planning a lightweight A/B rollout for model-quant-v2 + automatic fallback. want to validate the design before an RFC follow-up. key goals: preserve latency SLOs, avoid KV prefix cache thrash, and keep cost bounded. thoughts?

jia: love this. couple tradeoffs: do we do request-level fallback (retry to base model) or token-level fallback (continue generation on base) — token-level is hard.

omar: +1 to request-level first. token-level requires stream stitching and is messy with different logits. we should treat fallback as idempotent retry with a single attempt.

sam: idempotent retry seems simpler. concerns: session affinity — if we pin sessions to the quantized variant we may warm caches but then failover will migrate a lot of KV state.

lina: for affinity, consider short affinity TTL (e.g., 30s) and a probe-based refresh. also mark affinity entries with model-variant tag so metrics reflect cache-hit correlation.

jia: agreed. also suggest probe oracles: lightweight probe requests that mimic 90th pctile tail (few tokens) to observe latency delta without impacting users. run probes from canary nodes to both variants.

omar: we should separate routing policy from health decisions. routing decides where to send traffic; health decides fallback eligibility. both should be exposed via a control-plane API so Dedicated/private customers can tweak.

sam: makes sense. what about cache-priming? quantized model may have different KV cache shapes (quantization packs). We can prime via synthetic prefixes for top user funnels.

lina: synthetic priming + passive priming (copy popular prefixes from base->quantized) is good. but copying must be gated by a checksum/version to avoid corrupting alignment.

jia: propose a minimal rollout policy config; keep it small for now:

```json
{
  "variant_a": "model-base-v5",
  "variant_b": "model-quant-v2",
  "traffic_percent_b": 10,
  "affinity_ttl_seconds": 30,
  "max_retry_attempts": 1,
  "fallback_conditions": ["5xx", "latency>500ms", "generation_timeout"],
  "probe_interval_seconds": 15
}
```

sam: this captures the essentials. we need an explicit budget for extra tokens/cost from fallbacks. maybe a token_budget_per_minute per-customer.

omar: yes — and quorum logic for metrics (e.g., require 100 probes or 10m of traffic) before promoting or scaling up. promotion should be manual for enterprise flows.

lina: observability hooks: we need per-request tag with rollout_version, fallback_reason, pre-warm_hit. add cost attribution to trace spans.

jia: also think about graceful degradation: if quantized model produces bad quality signals (BLEU/ROUGE proxy or eval hooks), auto-evict from routing and switch to degraded-mode that only serves safe endpoints. keep deterministic rollout history.

sam: operational playbook:
- start with 1–5% random routing, affinity TTL 30s
- enable probes & passive priming
- watch latency and "fallback_rate" for 10m
- if fallback_rate > 1% or latency delta > 100ms, pause
- if sustained good for 1h and probe success > 95%, bump to 25%

lia (typo) — oops, meant lina: add alerting on fallback_rate per-customer and global token-budget burn.

deploy-bot: Canary started: model-quant-v2 on pool-us-west-2, 10% traffic, probes enabled.

sam: nice — can we add an endpoint to fetch current rollout state? e.g., /rollouts/{id}/state that returns counters and last probe results. customers on Dedicated should be able to query it.

omar: yeah, expose via control plane and emit events to event-stream so console and webhooks can consume.

jia: one last concern: latency SLO chasing — fallbacks can create cascading load on base model. add a circuit-breaker that temporarily rejects fallbacks when base-model CPU/GPU utilization > 80% and instead route to a tiny model or return a polite rate-limit response.

lina: +1. small-model degrade path should be defined per-route. document quality expectations for that degrade path.

sam: ok i'll draft a short RFC with the config schema, rollout playbook, and operation runbook. thanks all — if no objections i'll spin it up tomorrow and link to this thread. :thumbsup:
